# Refusal: the support-bundle tests cannot build a bundle without a live Postgres

The item states its own stopping condition:

> If the existing tests cannot build a bundle without a live Postgres, say so
> and stop rather than introducing a mock — that is a correct outcome and a
> different item.

That condition holds. Nothing else in the item is ambiguous; this one fact
rules out delivering a test that "passes now" under the stated check.

## What I found

**The only support-bundle assertions live inside an ignored Postgres test.**
Every existing reference to the bundle in `crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs`
is inside `postgres_auth_csrf_roles_and_connection_persistence`
(`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:15195`), which is declared:

```rust
#[tokio::test]
#[ignore = "requires RDPAPP_TEST_DATABASE_URL"]
async fn postgres_auth_csrf_roles_and_connection_persistence() {
    let database_url = env::var("RDPAPP_TEST_DATABASE_URL")
        .expect("set RDPAPP_TEST_DATABASE_URL to a disposable Postgres database");
```

Its own doc comment says the ignore is deliberate: "Keeping this ignored in the
ordinary unit suite makes `cargo test` independent of a developer's local
Docker setup." The bundle assertions run at
`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:15841`-`15876`, including the existing
`assert!(!support_bundle_text.contains("rotated-secret"))` — the closest
neighbour to what this item asks for.

**The fixture is a real database, not an in-memory one.** That test builds
`Repository::new(pool, test_vault())` from a `PgPoolOptions::connect(...)`,
migrates, `TRUNCATE`s, and calls `app_with_repository(...)`
(`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:11996`… declared at
`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:10996`). `just test-integration` (justfile
line 25) exists precisely to bring up `docker compose ... postgres` for it.

**There is no non-Postgres route to a serialised bundle.**
`download_support_bundle` (`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:6915`) obtains its
data through `repository(&state)?`
(`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:6252`), which returns the concrete
`Repository` struct (`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:95`) or a
`503 repository_unavailable` when `state.repository` is `None`. `Repository` is
a struct over a `PgPool`, not a trait, so it cannot be substituted. The snippet
rows the bundle maps from come from
`Repository::snippets` (`crates/rdpapp-gateway/src/main.rs:2807`), a direct
`sqlx::query("SELECT id,name,text,revision FROM snippets ...")` against
`self.pool`. Creating a workspace snippet with a sentinel `text` and then
serialising a bundle for that workspace — exactly what the item asks — therefore
requires a live Postgres.

## Why this collides with the item as written

- Scope point 2 requires the test to **pass now**. The judging check is
  `cargo test -p rdpapp-models -p rdpapp-sessions -p rdpapp-gateway`, which does
  not run `#[ignore]`d tests and does not set `RDPAPP_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. A test
  written against the neighbouring fixture would be skipped, not passed.
- Scope point 4 requires reusing the neighbours' fixture rather than
  introducing a new one, and point 3 forbids any production change. So the two
  routes that would make the test run under the stated command are both closed:
  a fake/in-memory repository is the mock the item rules out, and making
  `Repository` substitutable is a production change.

## What the different item would be

Adding an `#[ignore = "requires RDPAPP_TEST_DATABASE_URL"]` sentinel test beside
`postgres_auth_csrf_roles_and_connection_persistence`, guarding the bundle under
`just test-integration` rather than under `cargo test`. That is a real guard and
it is not a mock, but it does not satisfy "passes now" against the check this
item is judged by, so I have left it undone rather than quietly redefining the
scope. Deciding whether the integration suite is the right home for this guard
is the call the follow-up item should make.

No other change is left in the working tree.
